primary_topics: Address at Angeles University Foundation on receiving an honorary Doctor of Laws degree, October 5, 2006 -- CJP's return to Pampanga; the new AUF College of Law with Justice Jose Vitug as founding dean

Pampanga's resilience: Clark Air Base pullout, Mt. Pinatubo 1991 eruption -- both feared as economic regressions; the Clark Special Economic Zone as the bouncing back; 'a testimonial to the Pampanguenos' resilience and fortitude'

Jose Abad Santos as the supreme embodiment of the four Ins: the fifth CJ; born San Fernando, Pampanga; refused to cooperate with Japanese captors; 'Don't cry... It is a rare opportunity to die for one's country, and not everybody is given that chance' -- died a martyr
CJP's departing legacy for Pampangueño magistrates: energized breed championing the four Ins, battling ACID, and safeguarding liberty and nurturing prosperity
sub_topics: Pampanga's development: 'during the one-and-a-half hour drive from the Supreme Court to Angeles City... Pampanga is in the cusp of development. Yet, not too long ago, many feared its economic regression after the Americans pulled out from Clark Air Base, and after the destructive eruption of Mt. Pinatubo in 1991. Since then, the Clark Special Economic Zone has replaced the American base.'

AUF College of Law: 'the establishment of the AUF College of Law heeds the call for quality legal education in Central Luzon. With retired Supreme Court Justice Jose C. Vitug, a fellow Kapampangan and dear friend, as its founding dean, I am confident that soon its fine young graduates will be among those who will land on the coveted top ten places in the toughest bar examinations.'

Abad Santos biography: born San Fernando, Pampanga, February 19, 1886; justice SC 1932; secretary of justice 1938; captured by Japanese in Barili, Cebu, April 11, 1942; 'adamantly refused to cooperate with the military conquerors or to provide them with any vital information about the resistance movement'; before execution: 'Don't cry. What is the matter with you? Show these people that you are brave. It is a rare opportunity to die for one's country, and not everybody is given that chance.'

Four Ins as Abad Santos's governing standard: 'Chief Justice Abad Santos lived and died by an ideal magistrate's standards, which I have referred to in many past speeches as the four Ins: independence, integrity, industry and intelligence. Integrity is not limited to mere honesty and truthfulness; it entails acting in accordance with what is true and honest regardless of personal consequences. Integrity requires the moral courage to stand for one's convictions against all odds.'

Two months to retirement: 'In about two months, I shall bid adieu to the judiciary of our country. I shall leave with the conviction that I have tried my best to live up to the expectations of our cabalens and of all Filipinos in general.'

Closing: 'I look forward to retirement with tranquility and contentment over the thought that I shall leave behind an energized breed of Pampangueño magistrates who personify the four Ins; who continue to battle the ACID problems of our justice system; and who champion the loftier cause of safeguarding liberty and nurturing prosperity!'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered October 5, 2006 at Angeles University Foundation on receiving an honorary Doctor of Laws degree -- with retired Justice Jose C. Vitug (fellow Kapampangan) as founding dean of the new AUF College of Law -- this address by CJP opens by noting Pampanga's development: 'Pampanga is in the cusp of development. Yet, not too long ago, many feared its economic regression after the Americans pulled out from Clark Air Base, and after the destructive eruption of Mt. Pinatubo in 1991. Since then, the Clark Special Economic Zone has replaced the American base' -- 'a testimonial to the Pampanguenos' resilience and fortitude.' He introduces the new AUF College of Law with Vitug as dean and expresses confidence its graduates will reach the bar's top ten. He presents Jose Abad Santos as the supreme embodiment of the four Ins: 'born in San Fernando, Pampanga, February 19, 1886; became SC justice in 1932; secretary of justice in 1938; captured by Japanese in Barili, Cebu, April 11, 1942; adamantly refused to cooperate with the military conquerors; before execution, his parting words to his son: Don't cry. What is the matter with you? Show these people that you are brave. It is a rare opportunity to die for one's country, and not everybody is given that chance. Thus, he died a martyr and hero.' CJP's interpretation: 'Chief Justice Abad Santos lived and died by an ideal magistrate's standards, which I have referred to in many past speeches as the four Ins: independence, integrity, industry and intelligence. Integrity is not limited to mere honesty and truthfulness; it entails acting in accordance with what is true and honest regardless of personal consequences. Integrity requires the moral courage to stand for one's convictions against all odds.' Two months from retirement: 'I look forward to retirement with tranquility and contentment over the thought that I shall leave behind an energized breed of Pampangueño magistrates who personify the four Ins; who continue to battle the ACID problems of our justice system; and who champion the loftier cause of safeguarding liberty and nurturing prosperity! Dacal pung salamat.'
